q: 1. Cleaning period for slow sand filter is taken as .............
explain: Slow sand filters have a long filter run, typically requiring cleaning only once every 1 to 3 months depending on raw water turbidity.

q: 2. Rate of filtration of a slow sand filter ranges from .............
explain: Slow sand filters operate at a very low rate, usually between 100 to 200 liters per hour per square meter of filter area.

q: 3. Slow sand filter is efficient to remove the bacteria from the raw water to an extent of .............
explain: Due to the Schmutzdecke (biological layer), slow sand filters are exceptionally good at removing bacteria, often achieving 98% to 99% removal.

q: 4. Slow sand filter is more efficient for the removal of .............
explain: While they remove some turbidity and odour, the primary technical advantage of slow sand filters is their superior bacterial removal capability.

q: 5. In rapid sand filter .............
options: raw water from the sources is supplied
raw water passed through coagulation tank is supplied
explain: Rapid sand filters cannot handle high turbidity alone; they must be preceded by coagulation and sedimentation to be effective.

q: 6. The yield of a rapid sand filter is ............. to that of slow sand filter.
explain: Rapid sand filters have filtration rates (3000-6000 L/h/m²) that are roughly 30 times higher than slow sand filters (100-200 L/h/m²).

q: 7. An arrangement for back washing is provided in .............
explain: Backwashing (reversing water flow to expand the sand bed) is the standard method for cleaning rapid sand filters.

q: 8. In a rapid sand filter, the filter head varies from .............
explain: Rapid sand filters are designed to operate with a head loss of up to 3 to 4 meters before they require backwashing.

q: 9. Cleaning of rapid sand filters is done by .............
options: scraping the top layer of filter media
explain: Unlike slow sand filters which are scraped, rapid sand filters are cleaned by forceful backwashing with water and sometimes air.

q: 10. Cleaning period for a rapid sand filter is taken as .............
explain: Because they operate at much higher rates, rapid sand filters clog quickly and typically need cleaning every 1 to 3 days.

q: 11. rapid sand filter can remove bacteria upto an extent of .............
explain: Rapid sand filters are less efficient at bacterial removal (80-90%) than slow sand filters because they lack the biological 'dirty skin' layer.

q: 12. Rapid sand filter can remove turbidity from water upto an extend of .............
explain: Rapid sand filters are designed to handle and remove higher levels of turbidity compared to slow sand filters, provided pre-treatment is correct.

q: 13. pressure filters are not used for treating municipal water supplies, because .............
options: the rate of filtration is high
the overall plant capacity is small
they are efficient in the removal of turbidity and bacteria
explain: Pressure filters are compact but not scalable for massive municipal demands; their design is better suited for smaller, localized applications.

q: 14. Pressure filters are best suited for .............
explain: Due to their high rate and enclosed design, they are ideal for swimming pools, industrial sites, and small colonies.

q: 15. The process of killing pathogenic bacteria from water is called .............
explain: Disinfection specifically targets the destruction of disease-causing organisms to make water safe for consumption.

q: 16. The most commonly used disinfectant for drinking water throughout the world is .............
explain: Chlorine is used globally because it is effective, provides a residual effect in pipes, and is relatively inexpensive.

q: 17. The ideal method of disinfection of swimming pool water is by .............
explain: Ozone is a very powerful oxidant that leaves no unpleasant 'chlorine smell' or taste, making it ideal for high-end swimming pools.

q: 18. The amount of residual chlorine in treated water is determined by the .............
explain: Orthotolidine is the common field test, while Iodometric and Amperometric titration are used for more precise laboratory measurements.

q: 19. The time of contact for chlorination should be at least .............
explain: Chlorine requires a 'contact time' (usually 20-30 minutes) to successfully react with and kill microorganisms.

q: 20. The treatment of water with only chlorine is known as .............
explain: Plain chlorination is the process of adding chlorine to raw water that has not received any other treatment (like filtration or sedimentation).

q: 21. Pre-chlorination .............
explain: Adding chlorine at the start of the treatment process helps oxidize organic matter, improving the performance of subsequent stages.

q: 22. The prevent formation of crystalline hydrates of 'Ice' of chlorine, the chlorine supply cylinders are kept at a temperature from .............
explain: Maintaining a moderate temperature prevents the chlorine from forming solid hydrates which could block valves and pipes.

q: 23. Crystalline hydrates of 'Ice' of chlorine are formed at a temperature of .............
explain: At temperatures below 9.6°C, chlorine can form solid yellow crystals (chlorine ice) in the presence of water.

q: 24. The apparatus used for feeding chlorine into water is called .............
explain: A chlorinator is a mechanical device designed to regulate and inject precise amounts of chlorine gas or liquid into a water stream.

q: 25. When the chlorine is added beyond the break point, the process of treating the water is known as .............
explain: Super-chlorination involves adding high doses of chlorine to effectively treat heavily polluted water or during epidemics.

q: 26. The process of removing excess chlorine from water is called .............
explain: De-chlorination is necessary when the residual chlorine level is too high for safe or pleasant consumption.

q: 27. The process of dechlorination is followed by .............
explain: After super-chlorination and de-chlorination, a small 'post-chlorination' dose is often added to maintain a safe residual in the network.

q: 28. The amount of chlorine used for plain chlorination of water is about .............
explain: Plain chlorination typically requires around 0.5 mg/L (ppm) to achieve proper disinfection in relatively clean raw water.

q: 29. The most commonly used chemical for dechlorination of water is .............
explain: Sodium thiosulphate is the standard chemical used to neutralize excess chlorine rapidly.

q: 30. In orthotolodine test, safe residual for drinking water is indicated by .............
explain: A lemon-yellow color in an OT test indicates a safe residual chlorine level of approximately 0.1 to 0.2 ppm.

q: 31. Bleaching power is .............
explain: Bleaching powder is chemically known as Calcium Hypochlorite, $Ca(OCl)_2$.

q: 32. The percentage of chlorine in fresh bleaching power is .............
explain: Commercial 'fresh' bleaching powder usually contains about 30% to 35% available chlorine.

q: 33. The temporary hardness in water is caused due to the salts like .............
explain: Temporary (carbonate) hardness is caused by bicarbonates and carbonates of calcium and magnesium.

q: 34. The permanent hardness in water is caused due to the salts like .............
explain: Non-carbonate (permanent) hardness is caused by chlorides, nitrates, and sulphates of calcium and magnesium.

q: 35. The temporary hardness due to calcium bicarbonates can be removed by .............
explain: Boiling causes bicarbonates to decompose into insoluble carbonates, which then precipitate out of the water.

q: 36. The permanent hardness of water can be removed by .............
explain: The Zeolite (base-exchange) process is highly effective at removing both temporary and permanent hardness.

q: 37. By lime soda process, hardness can be reduced to less than .............
explain: While Zeolite reaches zero hardness, the chemical Lime-Soda process typically reduces it to about 30-50 ppm.

q: 38. The lime soda process of water softening .............
options: is suitable for turbid and acidic water
explain: The Lime-Soda process provides several side benefits, including disinfection (due to high pH) and assisting in coagulation.
Natural or synthetic zeolites are complex compounds of Sodium Aluminum Silicate used for ion exchange.

q: 40. In zeolite process .............
options: water of varying quality can be treated
ferrous and manganese from water are removed
explain: The Zeolite process is clean (no sludge), versatile, and removes other metallic ions besides hardness-causing ones.

q: 41. Zeolite process is also known as .............
explain: The terms 'Base Exchange' and 'Cation Exchange' are synonymous with the Zeolite softening process.

q: 42. The hydrants are used for tapping water from mains for .............
explain: Fire hydrants provide high-volume access to municipal water for emergency use and maintenance tasks like street or sewer flushing.

q: 43. The minimum size of as fire hydrants is
explain: For effective fire fighting, a minimum diameter of 10 cm is generally required to ensure sufficient water discharge and pressure.

q: 44. The valve provided on the suction pipe in a tube well is
explain: A reflux valve (also known as a check valve or foot valve in suction) is used to prevent the backflow of water when the pump stops, keeping the pump primed.

q: 45. The type of joint to be used in pipes depends upon the
explain: Pipe joint selection must consider the pipe material, the pressure it will sustain, and the stability or movement of the ground/supports.

q: 46. The pipe joint commonly used in pumping stations is
explain: Flanged joints are preferred in pumping stations and treatment plants because they are easy to assemble and disassemble for maintenance.

q: 47. In order to control the flow of water through pipes, a ............... is provided.
explain: Gate valves (also known as sluice valves) are used to start or stop the flow of water; they are used as isolation valves rather than for throttling.

q: 48. In order to prevent water to flow back opposite direction, we shall use a
explain: Reflux valves are used specifically to ensure water flows in the intended direction only, preventing reversal.

q: 49. The capacity of the pumps is normally expressed as
explain: Pump capacity (discharge) can be expressed in various units depending on the scale, including L/min, m³/day, or L/hr.

q: 50. For an area developed in haphazard way, the types of layout for the distribution of pipes is
explain: The dead-end system (tree system) is used for unplanned/haphazard cities as it follows the irregular road patterns and is cheap.
